about: Apps, receivers, hosted services, hardware, production tools and docs for IRL streaming, one entry per product. Fields and rules: https://github.com/irl-commons/irl-commons/blob/main/data/README.md

services.name: Bond Bunny
services.description: Android app that takes an SRT stream from another app on the phone and sends it to an SRTLA receiver over several connections; from LifeStreamer's developer.

services.name: IRL+ Cast
services.description: Android app for going live from the phone's cameras, USB cameras or network cameras. It sends over SRT, RTMP, SRTLA or IRL+'s own BOND, and bonds cellular, Wi-Fi and Moblink relays.

services.name: IRL+ Chat
services.description: Android chat manager for Twitch, Kick and YouTube, with text-to-speech, OBS control and the encoder's live bitrate. Free.

services.name: IRL Pro
services.description: Android app for IRL streaming, with SRTLA bonding and a free bonding service.

services.name: Larix Broadcaster
services.description: Streaming apps for Android and iOS, by Softvelum.

services.name: LifeStreamer
services.description: Android app with USB video in, SRTLA bonding and a Moblink server.

services.name: MediaSrvr
services.description: Runs an RTMP server on an Android phone, so an action camera can send its picture to the phone; made mainly for use with LifeStreamer.

services.name: Moblin
services.description: A free, open-source iPhone app for IRL streaming, with SRTLA and RIST bonding. It can film with several of the phone's cameras at once, picture-in-picture, and its ingests (RTMP, SRT(LA), RIST and WHIP servers) take streams from other phones and cameras into a scene. Mobcam makes the phone a low-latency webcam over USB, for example as a camera in OBS. On iPad it takes UVC (USB-C) cameras. Its OBS remote control changes scenes, starts and stops the stream and mutes inputs.

services.name: Moblink
services.description: Uses spare Android phones as extra bonding connections; the same works from iPhones running Moblin.

services.name: OBS Blade
services.description: "The open source remote for OBS Studio, on iPhone, iPad and Android." Free, with a paid Pro tier.

services.name: RealtimeIRL
services.description: iPhone and Android apps that share your live location to rtirl.com; the iPhone app has privacy zones for places you don't want published. Needs an rtirl.com account; in-app purchases for extra features. By Muxable.

services.name: TVU Go
services.description: One phone app combining cellular, Wi-Fi and tethered phones, by subscription.

services.name: BELABOX Cloud
services.description: Hosted receivers for BELABOX users, as a sponsor perk.

services.name: doink.tv
services.description: A free service with drop protection and connection bonding.

services.name: IRL+ BOND
services.description: IRL+'s own encrypted bonding protocol, separate from SRT and SRTLA. You send with IRL+'s bond-send app or the IRL+ phone app, to a receiver run by IRL+ or a receiver host. Free trials.

services.name: irl-srt-server
services.description: The IRL-focused fork of SRT Live Server, with SRTLA bonding support and a stats page.

services.name: MediaMTX
services.description: A ready-to-use live media server and proxy for SRT, RTMP, WebRTC, RTSP and more. It takes plain SRT but not SRTLA, so in a bonded setup it sits behind an SRTLA receiver.

services.name: OpenIRL srtla-receiver
services.description: A self-hosted SRTLA receiver, the core of the OpenIRL toolkit: several streams with their own publish and play keys, set up in the browser, with a stats endpoint per stream that NOALBS supports. A different project from Halveknots' OpenIRL under Production.

services.name: Speedify
services.description: An app that combines several internet connections (Wi-Fi, cellular, Ethernet, satellite) for any traffic, by subscription.

services.name: SRT
services.description: Secure Reliable Transport, the open protocol that SRTLA is built on.

services.name: srtla
services.description: The original SRT link-aggregation sender and receiver; its README marks the receiver as unsupported and no longer developed.

services.name: BELABOX
services.description: An IRL encoder on small boards with modems; its control screen, belaUI, is GPL-3.0.

services.name: CeraLive
services.description: "a live-streaming system you build yourself", built on open source. Its control panel, bonding sender and receivers are public on GitHub; the streaming engine on the device isn't.

services.name: Dejero EnGo
services.description: Professional mobile transmitters that blend all available connections, for broadcast.

services.name: Haivision Pro
services.description: Mobile video transmitters over bonded cellular and IP, for broadcast.

services.name: IRL+ store
services.description: 3D-printed cases for ROCK 5B+ and Orange Pi 5+ boards, modem cooling and bag mods, made to order in the UK.

services.name: IRLbox
services.description: A ready-made encoder system for Orange Pi and Radxa boards, on Ubuntu, with SRT, RTMP and RIST and a web dashboard. Free download in open beta; no source code or licence is published, only its docs on GitHub.

services.name: LiveU Solo
services.description: Bonded encoders for creators, on LiveU's LRT bonding, by subscription.

services.name: Starlink
services.description: Satellite internet; joins a backpack as one more link. Best with a clear view of the sky; in motion it needs the right plan and mount.

services.name: Teradek Prism Mobile
services.description: A camera-back encoder that bonds cellular and other connections; needs a Teradek subscription or licence.

services.name: TVU One
services.description: A broadcast-grade 5G transmitter.

services.name: UnlimitedIRL
services.description: Ready-built IRL backpacks and accessories, with expert help.

services.name: YoloBox Ultra
services.description: An all-in-one camera encoder with a screen and HDMI inputs; bonding is a paid service.

services.name: IRL+ Video Mixer
services.description: Mixes HDMI and USB cameras, a phone feed and overlays into one picture on the box itself. For BELABOX setups on a ROCK 5B+ or Orange Pi 5+. An independent add-on with its own support. Free, with paid remote access.

services.name: IRLhosting
services.description: Cloud OBS servers for IRL streamers, with SRTLA bonding and disconnect protection; its receivers and SimpleStreamer are listed separately.

services.name: IRLToolkit
services.description: Cloud production with overlays and drop protection; several inputs on the bigger plan.

services.name: NOALBS
services.description: Switches OBS scenes automatically when the bitrate drops.

services.name: OBS IRL Source
services.description: An OBS source for receiving IRL streams over SRT, RTMP or RIST that recovers on its own after a dropout and repairs audio gaps.

services.name: OBS Studio
services.description: The open-source production software most of this plugs into.

services.name: OpenIRL (Halveknots)
services.description: "Local-first Rust control plane for IRL streaming": OBS automation, ingest, fallback and self-hosted relay workflows. A different project from the OpenIRL srtla-receiver under Bonding.

services.name: Streamer.bot
services.description: Automation for live streams on Twitch, YouTube and Kick, with OBS Studio control (OBS WebSocket 4 and 5) and Stream Deck control.

services.name: BELABOX wiki
services.description: Modems, accessories, power banks.

services.name: CeraLive docs
services.description: Hardware lists, modems and audio devices.

services.name: IRLToolkit knowledge base
services.description: Ingests, encoders, OBS WebSocket.

services.name: Moblin README and features
services.description: The app's own feature list.

services.name: IRLwhatever
services.description: An all-in-one Android app for streaming IRL from one phone. It has phone and USB cameras, scenes with picture-in-picture, and SRTLA, RIST and SRT with adaptive bitrate. It can use spare phones as extra connections through Moblink. It also has Twitch and Kick chat with text-to-speech, overlays and alerts, OBS scene switching and a browser remote. Licence not stated.

services.name: IRLrelays
services.description: Hosted receivers that carry your stream to your own OBS, over SRT, SRTLA, RIST or RTMP, with stats a scene switcher can read. The region can change and the relay ID stays. Paid.

services.name: SimpleStreamer
services.description: A hosted server that passes your stream on to up to three platforms without re-encoding and shows a BRB screen when the signal drops. Takes SRTLA, SRT, RIST and RTMP; H.264 only. Paid.

services.name: NoDrop
services.description: IRLToolkit's hosted drop protection, controlled with commands in a chat channel: shows an image, a looping video or a second feed while yours is gone. Its output starts separately. Paid.

services.name: NOALBS Cloud
services.description: The hosted NOALBS: reads your receiver's stats URL and switches OBS through one browser source, with a phone dashboard and chat commands. Paid plans; can also be self-hosted.

services.name: Smooth Media Source
services.description: An OBS source for remote RTMP, SRT and RIST feeds that rebuilds its audio buffer after a dropout and reconnects when the feed drops. Windows, OBS 32.0 to 32.2.

services.name: moo RIST receiver
services.description: Self-hosted RIST receivers for IRL streaming, built for several machine types; its README names IRLbox and IRLwhatever as RIST senders.

services.name: librtmp2-server
services.description: A self-hosted RTMP, RTMPS and Enhanced RTMP server for OBS and FFmpeg, with live stats; NOALBS reads it as the OpenRTMP server type. A new project, started in June 2026.

services.name: VDO.Ninja
services.description: Brings remote video feeds into OBS over WebRTC, for example a phone as a guest camera, from a browser.

services.name: BelaBot
services.description: A chat bot that controls a BELABOX's belaUI through BELABOX Cloud, from the NOALBS project. Last updated in April 2025.

services.name: Syncer.live
services.description: A shared clock page to show on two or more feeds at once, to see how far apart they arrive and line them up.

services.name: Twitch
services.description: Live streaming platform that receives broadcasts and shows them to viewers.

services.name: BELABOX cloud stream servers
services.description: Hosted production with transcoding, drop protection, web overlays, scene switching and picture-in-picture, streaming to platforms without running OBS.

services.description: Controls a BELABOX encoder over the internet without a direct local network connection.
